:::{#exr-wilks-taylor}
#### Quadratic approximation to the log-likelihood

Let $\param$ be a scalar parameter,
and suppose the MLE $\hthml$ maximizes $\llik$
at an interior point of the parameter space,
where $\llik$ is twice differentiable.
Use a second-order Taylor expansion around $\hthml$
to approximate $\llik(\param_0)$
in terms of $\llik(\hthml)$ and the [Hessian](#def-hessian) $\hess(\hthml)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-wilks-taylor}

The MLE maximizes $\llik$ at an interior point,
so $\score(\hthml) = 0$.
A second-order Taylor expansion of $\llik(\param_0)$ around $\hthml$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\llik(\param_0)
&\approx \llik(\hthml) + \score(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)
 + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{(Taylor expansion)}\\
&= \llik(\hthml) + 0 \cdot (\param_0 - \hthml)
 + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{($\score(\hthml) = 0$)}\\
&= \llik(\hthml) + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\param_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
